name: Art Nouveau monogram
region: Belgium, the Netherlands, Austria and France
summary: Interlaced initials and lettering drawn as one ornament, inside a frame of whiplash curves and plant forms. Publishers, societies and workshops used it as a vignette on books, journals and printed matter.

philosophy.core_thesis: The letters and the ornament are one drawing: a mark grows like a plant from one line, and the hand of the artist shows in each curve.
design_principles: Interlace 1–3 initials so that their strokes share at least one stem or one bowl.
Draw each curve as a whiplash: an S-curve whose radius changes along the stroke by a factor of 3 or more.
Close the mark in a frame of plant stems or tendrils, with the frame line 1.5–2 times the letter stroke.
Draw custom capitals with small x-heights, high crossbars and open, rounded counters; no typeface from a foundry.
Keep stroke contrast low, 1.5:1 to 3:1, so that the mark prints in one ink as a block.
Fit the mark to a vertical rectangle near 3:4 or a square, centred on a vertical axis.
anti_patterns: Straight-sided geometric letters from a typeface
Rigid circles and squares as the only frame
Letters that float apart with no shared stroke

construction.grid: No modular grid. One vertical axis and a frame that fits a 3:4 or 1:1 rectangle; the lettering sits on 2–4 baselines inside it.
construction.geometry: Freehand curves of changing radius; few straight lines, and no arc from a compass.
construction.stroke_rule: Letter strokes at 4–7% of the mark height; frame lines at 1.5–2 times the letter stroke.
construction.symmetry: Mirror symmetry for the frame; the interlaced initials break it in the centre.
construction.detail_floor: Gaps between interlaced strokes of at least 1.5% of the mark height, so that the interlace survives letterpress.

form.silhouette: A vertical rectangle near 3:4, a square or a pointed oval, with tendrils that touch the frame corners.
form.ornament: Whiplash tendrils, buds, leaves, dots in groups of three, and stylised water or flowers in the frame.
form.letterforms: Hand-drawn capitals with high crossbars, bulging bowls and small serifs; letter spacing even and wide, often 10–20% of the cap height.

colour.strategy: One dark ink on a toned paper; a second muted ink, sage, ochre or dull red, for the frame or the ground.
colour.reversal_rule: The mark is drawn as one ink, so it reverses white on dark with no change; open the interlace gaps by 10% for a reversal.

reproduction.clear_space: 0.2 × the mark height on each side, measured from the outermost tendril.
reproduction.media: Letterpress line blocks, book covers, title pages, stamps for silver and ceramics.

emotion.target_response: Grace and craft: the viewer sees a hand-drawn, living line and feels care and taste.

avoid_when: The brief needs a technical, neutral or rational tone.
The mark must read at 16 px.

modifiers.how: Keep the custom letters and the even spacing; drop the frame and the tendrils, and set the letters in one weight on one baseline.
Keep the frame; add a pictorial device, banners and a second typeface.
